headline: GASKET SLEEPS SOUND — TILL TWO STRANGERS ROLL INTO TOWN
subhead: A blessed hush falls over Gasket today, and the Sheriff dares to enjoy it — right up until two new sets of boots kick dust at the town line.
body:
Friends, I write to you this morning a rested man. No iron balls went hurtling. No fists went flying. Not one soul marched out past the town line to go looking for trouble with the wild engines in the wastes, and for one whole day Gasket got to be what it was always meant to be: quiet. I sat on my porch, oiled my knee — a man's joints do stiffen up something fierce out here in the dry air, mind you, nothing more sinister than that — and I listened to nothing but wind. It was glorious.

But don't go thinking I've gone soft on optimism, because peace in this town never holds its breath for long. Two new faces rolled in and signed the register this week — IRON-0577 and, I kid you not, STEEL BALLS. Now I don't know what kind of a name that is for an upstanding citizen to carry, and I'll not speculate on the constitution of anybody's insides, but you mark my words: nobody rides into Gasket unless they've got a grudge, a gauntlet, or both. We'll see soon enough which one they brought.

My dear departed grandfather — flesh and blood, same as I am — used to say a quiet town is a town still worth saving. Fifty years since the last of the good honest folk packed up their wagons and left this place to rust, and still I find myself out here every morning, sweeping the porch of a town that isn't even mine to sweep anymore. Old habits. A lawman's curse.

So enjoy the hush while it lasts, Gasket. Two new gearheads are already asking around about the fight pits, and something tells this weary old sheriff his oil-can and I will not be resting long.
